lanes.convention: mirrors the established layout used by react-cypress-rwa and the Angular verticals: an immutable <app>-source corpus plus an <app>-runtime cell and an <app>-baseline cache under .versionless/cache/, and a mutable lane under .versionless/work/<app>/baseline. .versionless/ is gitignored, so none of these paths are tracked.
lanes.corpusImmutability: the whole corpus tree was made read-only (chmod -R a-w) immediately after extraction and was never written to; it is the reference the work lane is diffed against
lanes.npmCache: .versionless/cache/angular-pigallery2-v1-7-0-baseline/npm-cache (npm_config_cache, so the host user cache was not mutated)

eraCell.selected: node v10.24.1 (official darwin-x64 build), bundled npm 6.14.12
eraCell.policyForSelection: the Node 10 line is the only version the application's own three statements agree on: engines '>= 6.9 <11.0', the Docker base node:10-stretch (debian and arm32v7), and the lower of the two Travis entries. 10.24.1 is the final release of that line. Node 11 was excluded because the app's engines ceiling '<11.0' is hard; no modern Node was substituted.
eraCell.sha256Source: https://nodejs.org/dist/v10.24.1/SHASUMS256.txt — the published line and the measured digest of the downloaded bytes agree
eraCell.hostFact: the host is arm64 macOS 26.5.1. There is no darwin-arm64 build of Node 10 (the line predates Apple silicon support), so the darwin-x64 binary executes through Rosetta 2 translation, which is present and active on this host. This is recorded as a host fact, not hidden: inside the cell process.platform/process.arch report darwin/x64, and that is what made npm resolve darwin-x64 native artefacts below.
eraCell.fallbackNote: no fallback was needed; the Node 10 cell executed normally under translation for the whole install and both builds

closureBreak.consequence: a verbatim `npm install` of this pin can no longer succeed from the public registry on any host or Node version. This is a property of the registry in 2026, not of this host.
closureBreak.notRepaired: no substitute package was invented, vendored or fabricated

nativeDependencies.sqlite3@4.0.9: OBTAINED. node-pre-gyp fetched a remote prebuilt binding for this exact cell: node_modules/sqlite3/lib/binding/node-v64-darwin-x64/node_sqlite3.node ('[sqlite3] Success: ... is installed via remote'). No source build was needed, and no Python 2 dependency was hit. The x64 ABI selection is a direct consequence of the Rosetta host fact above.
nativeDependencies.bcrypt@3.0.6: OBTAINED, optional. node-pre-gyp found no prebuilt for node-v64-darwin-x64 and fell back to a source build with node-gyp, which succeeded: node_modules/bcrypt/lib/binding/bcrypt_lib.node
nativeDependencies.sharp@0.22.1: OBTAINED, optional. Compiled from source against its bundled libvips: node_modules/sharp/build/Release/sharp.node
nativeDependencies.fsevents@1.2.9: OBTAINED, transitive/optional. Its S3 prebuilt bucket 404s for node-v64-darwin-x64, so all five copies fell back to a successful node-gyp source build
nativeDependencies.@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg@1.0.19 and @ffp: OBTAINED, optional. The darwin-x64 platform packages installed and their binaries were chmod'd u+x by their own postinstall; the linux-arm variants were skipped by npm as unsupported for this platform
nativeDependencies.gm@1.23.1: UNTESTED. gm is a wrapper around an external GraphicsMagick binary, and `gm` is not on this host's PATH ('gm not found'); an ImageMagick `convert` is present. The wrapper package installed; whether it can shell out was neither needed nor measured by this unit.
nativeDependencies.frontendNeed: none of the above is needed by the frontend build. sqlite3, bcrypt, sharp, gm and the ffmpeg/ffprobe installers are backend/optional dependencies; the Angular browser build reads only frontend/**, common/** and the devDependency toolchain. The question 'can the frontend baseline be built without backend natives' did not have to be answered as a fallback here, because every required native was in fact obtained.
nativeDependencies.summary: the required native (sqlite3) and every optional native except the external-binary wrapper gm were obtained for the era cell on this host. No native-dependency failure was recorded.

observationsForLaterUnits: index.html is not a static page: it is an EJS template containing <%= clientConfig.urlBase %> and a ServerInject script block filled by the backend at request time. Serving dist/ as plain static files will not produce a booting app; a witness path has to render it through the backend or supply the injected globals.
index.html also links two external stylesheets from CDNs (cdnjs bootstrap-switch 3.3.4 and unpkg leaflet 1.3.4). Any offline witness run will lose those styles.
the built output is en only, because CI=1 selected the app's own single-locale branch. fr, hu and ru locale builds exist in the app's gulpfile and were not run.
@angular/http@7.2.15 is still declared while Angular is 8.1.2; the production build completed anyway, so whatever imports it resolve at this pin.
sqlite3 arrived as a darwin-x64 prebuilt selected because of Rosetta; a native arm64 host or a Node 11+ ABI would not necessarily find one.
